qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global scale in ocean container shipping and APM Terminals provides network density, but newbuild vessel supply across global carrier alliances repeatedly dilutes returns. 10-year average ROIC sits in the 7-9% range (well below the 12% hurdle), with extreme earnings volatility and zero durable pricing power over shippers.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). Global container logistics and ocean liner giant. While operating scale and terminal infrastructure are substantial, ocean shipping is structurally commoditized and plagued by multi-year overcapacity cycles. Multi-cycle normalized ROIC of 7-9% is far below the 12% hurdle, with violent freight rate swings and lack of structural pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Maersk's 10-year historical ROIC averages 7-9% (median ~7.7%), with pre-COVID 2016-2020 ROIC fluctuating around 0-4% and post-pandemic 2023-2025 ROIC cooling to 3.5-4.2% despite Red Sea re-routing. Operating earnings depend heavily on global container freight rate indices (SCFI/CCFI) and uncoordinated newbuild vessel orders across alliances, preventing consistent economic value creation.
